questions.text: Which camera shot shows a character's face filling most of the frame?

options: Long shot
Establishing shot
Two-shot
Close-up
feedback: A long shot shows the whole body and some of the setting

questions.solution: A close-up frames the face, showing emotion in detail
questions.hint: The camera is very near the face

questions.text: Which camera movement turns the camera horizontally, left or right, while the camera stays in one place? Give the term.

feedback.tilt: A tilt moves the camera up or down
feedback.tracking shot: In a tracking shot the whole camera travels along
feedback.zoom: A zoom changes the lens, not the direction the camera points

questions.solution: A pan swivels the camera horizontally from a fixed position
questions.hint: It is a three-letter word

questions.text: What is an establishing shot used for?

options: Showing a character's tears in detail
Showing a conversation between two people
Showing where, and sometimes when, a scene takes place
Showing the end credits

questions.solution: An establishing shot, often an extreme long shot, sets up the location of a scene
questions.hint: It usually comes at the start of a scene

questions.text: Which camera angle looks up at a character from below, often making them seem powerful? Give the term.

feedback.high angle: A high angle looks down on a character, often making them seem weaker
feedback.high angle shot: A high angle looks down on a character, often making them seem weaker

questions.solution: A low-angle shot looks up at the subject, often suggesting power or threat
questions.hint: The camera is placed beneath the character's eye level

questions.text: What is a jump cut?

options: A smooth cut where an action continues across two shots
A gradual change from one image to another
An abrupt cut that makes time or the subject seem to jump forward
A shot taken from a helicopter
feedback: That is match on action
That is a dissolve

questions.solution: A jump cut is a sudden, noticeable cut within a scene that makes time appear to jump
questions.hint: The name tells you how it feels to watch

questions.text: Which editing technique cuts back and forth between two characters in a conversation, often over their shoulders?

options: Shot reverse shot
Montage
Jump cut
Cross-cutting

questions.solution: Shot reverse shot alternates between two characters, usually in conversation
questions.hint: One shot shows one character, the next shows the other

questions.text: What is the name for a series of short shots edited together to show time passing quickly, such as a training sequence? Give the term.
questions.solution: A montage compresses time by joining many short shots together
questions.hint: It comes from a French word meaning 'assembly'

questions.text: What is the difference between a tilt and a pan?

options: A tilt moves the camera from side to side; a pan moves it up or down
A tilt moves the camera up or down; a pan moves it from side to side
A tilt moves the whole camera along a track; a pan is a zoom
A tilt is an editing effect; a pan is a type of lighting
feedback: You have swapped them round

questions.solution: Both pivot from a fixed point: a tilt is vertical, a pan is horizontal
questions.hint: Think of nodding your head versus shaking it

questions.text: What is the difference between a zoom and a tracking shot?

options: A zoom moves the camera on rails; a tracking shot changes the lens
A zoom is always handheld; a tracking shot is always overhead
A zoom is a cut between shots; a tracking shot is a fade
A zoom changes the lens to magnify the image; in a tracking shot the camera itself moves
feedback: You have swapped them round

questions.solution: A zoom changes the focal length of the lens; a tracking shot physically moves the camera
questions.hint: Does the camera itself travel, or only the lens change?

questions.text: What is the name of the shot that shows exactly what a character is seeing, as if through their eyes? Give the term.
questions.solution: A point-of-view (POV) shot shows the scene from a character's viewpoint
questions.hint: Its abbreviation is three letters

questions.text: What is cross-cutting?

options: Cutting between two or more scenes happening at the same time in different places
Cutting between two people in one conversation
Using a fade to black between scenes
Cutting to a close-up of an object
feedback: That is shot reverse shot

questions.solution: Cross-cutting (parallel editing) switches between actions in different places, often to build tension
questions.hint: The scenes happen in different places

questions.text: Which editing rule says the camera should stay on one side of an imaginary line between two characters, so they keep the same left–right positions on screen? Give the name of the rule.

feedback.30-degree rule: The 30-degree rule is about moving the camera at least 30 degrees between shots of the same subject
feedback.30 degree rule: The 30-degree rule is about moving the camera at least 30 degrees between shots of the same subject

questions.solution: The 180-degree rule keeps the camera on one side of the line of action so screen positions stay consistent
questions.hint: The line cuts the circle around the actors in half

questions.text: What is the difference between a high angle and a bird's-eye view?

options: A high angle looks down from above eye level; a bird's-eye view looks straight down from overhead
A high angle looks up; a bird's-eye view looks down
A high angle is filmed from a plane; a bird's-eye view is filmed from the ground
They are the same: both look straight up at the sky

questions.solution: A high angle looks down at an angle; a bird's-eye view is directly overhead
questions.hint: Think about how steeply each one looks down

questions.text: Which editing technique cuts in the middle of a movement, so the action continues smoothly into the next shot? Give the term.
questions.solution: Match on action hides a cut by continuing a movement across two shots
questions.hint: The cut happens while someone is moving

questions.text: A director films a villain from a low angle as he stands over the hero. What does this suggest?

options: The villain is weak and vulnerable
The villain is powerful and threatening
The scene takes place at night
The hero is the villain's friend
feedback: A high angle would make him seem weak

questions.solution: Looking up at a character from a low angle makes them seem powerful and threatening
questions.hint: Think about how it feels to look up at someone

questions.text: In a thriller, the film cuts back and forth between a train speeding along and the hero running to warn the driver of a car stuck on the tracks. Which editing technique is this?

options: Shot reverse shot
Jump cut
Fade
Cross-cutting

questions.solution: Cutting between two actions in different places to build suspense is cross-cutting
questions.hint: Two different places, at the same time

questions.text: A camera mounted on a moving dolly travels alongside a character as she walks down a corridor. What type of shot is this? Give the term.

feedback.pan: A pan turns the camera from a fixed position; here the camera travels
feedback.zoom: A zoom changes the lens; here the camera itself moves

questions.solution: A tracking (dolly) shot moves the whole camera to follow the action
questions.hint: The dolly often runs on rails like a train

questions.text: A shot shows a character looking off-screen, then the film cuts to a shot of a letter on a table. What has the editor created?

options: Eyeline match
Jump cut
Montage
Dissolve

questions.solution: An eyeline match cuts from a character looking to what they are looking at
questions.hint: The second shot shows what the character sees

questions.text: One image slowly fades out while the next image fades in, so that for a moment both can be seen. What is this transition called? Give the term.

feedback.fade: A fade goes to or from a single colour, usually black; this transition overlaps two images
feedback.wipe: A wipe pushes one image off the screen with a moving edge

questions.solution: A dissolve overlaps two images, often to show time passing
questions.hint: Like sugar in tea, one image seems to melt away

questions.text: A horror film shows a scene with the camera tilted so the horizon is on a slant. What is this angle called?

options: Bird's-eye view
Dutch angle (canted angle)
Eye-level shot
Over-the-shoulder shot

questions.solution: A Dutch (canted) angle tilts the frame to create unease or disorientation
questions.hint: The frame is deliberately tilted

questions.text: Read this shot list: '1. Extreme long shot of a city at night. 2. Long shot of an apartment block. 3. Close-up of a woman at a window.' What is the effect of this sequence?

options: It shows the same moment from three random angles
It is a montage showing years passing
It moves from the location to a single character, guiding the audience in
It is a series of jump cuts that confuse the audience

questions.solution: The shots move from wide to close, establishing the city and then leading us to one character
questions.hint: Notice how the shot sizes change from 1 to 3

questions.text: Read this: 'Two characters argue. In shot 1 Ana is on the left of the frame; in shot 2 the camera has crossed the line and Ana now appears on the right.' Which rule has been broken, and what is the likely effect?

options: The 30-degree rule, which makes the shot last too long
The 180-degree rule, which may confuse the audience about where the characters are
The rule of thirds, which makes the image too bright
Match on action, which slows the scene down

questions.solution: Crossing the line breaks the 180-degree rule, so characters swap sides and the audience may feel disoriented
questions.hint: Which rule is about an imaginary line between characters?

questions.text: Read this: 'A long shot shows a car on a desert road; then a series of cuts shows the same car from the same angle in slightly different positions, each a few seconds later.' What type of cut is this? Give the term.

feedback.match cut: A match cut links two different shots by similar shapes or ideas
feedback.cutaway: A cutaway cuts to something else and then back

questions.solution: Cutting between near-identical shots of the same subject makes time jump forward
questions.hint: Think of the cut that makes time appear to leap forward

questions.text: Read this: a film's average shot length is 2 seconds in a chase scene and 12 seconds in a quiet dialogue scene. What does this show about the editing?

options: The chase uses longer takes than the dialogue scene
The dialogue scene has more cuts per minute
The editing is faster in the chase, building excitement
Both scenes are edited at the same pace

questions.solution: Shorter average shots mean more cuts and a faster editing pace, which builds excitement in the chase
questions.hint: A shorter average shot length means more cuts

questions.text: A shot begins focused on a phone in the foreground; then the focus shifts to a character's face in the background. What is this technique and its usual purpose?

options: Jump cut, used to show time moving on
Dutch angle, used to show unease
Crane shot, used to reveal a landscape
Pull focus (rack focus), moving the audience's attention between subjects

questions.solution: A pull (rack) focus shifts sharp focus within the shot, directing the audience's attention
questions.hint: Nothing is cut and the camera does not move: only the focus changes

questions.text: Explain how camera angles could be used to show the difference in power between a king and a frightened servant.

rubric.model_answer: The king could be filmed from a low angle so he seems to tower over the audience, suggesting power and authority. The servant could be filmed from a high angle, looking down on them, making them seem small and vulnerable. Cutting between these angles in shot reverse shot makes the difference in status clear.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: low angle for the king
1 mark: effect: power or dominance
1 mark: high angle for the servant
1 mark: effect: weakness or vulnerability, or how editing shows the contrast

questions.solution: Low angles suggest power; high angles suggest weakness
questions.hint: Think about where the camera is placed for each character

questions.text: Which statement about continuity editing is accurate?

options: It deliberately draws attention to every cut
It aims to make cuts invisible so the story flows logically in time and space
It is only used in documentaries
It means filming the whole film in one take

questions.solution: Continuity editing hides cuts, using rules such as the 180-degree rule and match on action
questions.hint: Think about the word 'continuity'

questions.text: Why might a director choose handheld camera work for a battle scene in a war film?

options: It creates a sense of chaos and realism, as if the audience is there
It makes the image perfectly smooth and calm
It is the only way to film outdoors
It makes the scene look like a painting

questions.solution: Shaky handheld camera work feels immediate and chaotic, like documentary footage
questions.hint: Think about how shaky footage feels to watch

questions.text: Which statement about the Kuleshov effect is accurate?

options: Audiences only notice the longest shot in a sequence
Editing has no effect on how a face is understood
Audiences read meaning from how shots are put together, not from each shot alone
It is a lighting technique used in horror films

questions.solution: Kuleshov showed that the same face seems to show different emotions depending on the shot placed next to it
questions.hint: It comes from early Soviet experiments with editing

questions.text: Why might a director use a long take instead of many cuts?

options: To make the scene feel faster and more fragmented
To build tension or realism by letting the action unfold without interruption
To hide every camera movement from the audience
Because long takes are required for every dialogue scene

questions.solution: A long take lets action unfold in real time, which can build tension and realism
questions.hint: What happens to time when there are no cuts?

questions.text: Why is the deep focus in Citizen Kane (1941) often discussed?

options: It was the first film ever shot in colour
It keeps foreground and background sharp at once, letting the audience choose where to look
It used only handheld cameras
It was the first film to use jump cuts

questions.solution: Citizen Kane's deep focus keeps near and far planes sharp at once, so several actions can be seen in one shot
questions.hint: Think about what 'deep' focus keeps sharp

questions.text: Explain how continuity editing makes a conversation scene easy to follow.

rubric.model_answer: An establishing shot first shows where the characters are. Shot reverse shot then cuts between the speakers, keeping to the 180-degree rule so each character stays on the same side of the screen. Eyeline matches make it clear who is looking at whom, and match on action hides cuts during movement. Together these make the cuts almost invisible.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: establishing shot sets up the space
1 mark: shot reverse shot
1 mark: the 180-degree rule keeps positions consistent
1 mark: eyeline match or match on action
1 mark: overall effect: invisible editing and a logical flow

questions.solution: Establishing shots, shot reverse shot, the 180-degree rule and eyeline matches keep a conversation clear
questions.hint: Follow the scene from its first shot to the cuts between speakers

questions.text: What does mise-en-scène mean?

options: The order in which shots are edited
Everything placed in the frame, such as setting, props, costume, lighting and performance
The music added after filming
The camera's movement during a shot
feedback: That is editing

questions.solution: Mise-en-scène is everything in front of the camera: setting, props, costume, lighting and performance
questions.hint: It is a French phrase about what is put into the scene

questions.text: What is the term for sound whose source exists in the world of the film, such as dialogue or a car horn the characters can hear? Give the term.

feedback.non-diegetic: Non-diegetic sound comes from outside the story world, such as the film score
feedback.non-diegetic sound: Non-diegetic sound comes from outside the story world, such as the film score

questions.solution: Diegetic sound comes from within the story world, so the characters can hear it
questions.hint: The word comes from the Greek for 'narrative', meaning the story world

questions.text: Which lighting style is bright, with few shadows, and is often used in comedies and musicals?

options: Low-key lighting
Chiaroscuro
Underlighting
High-key lighting
feedback: Low-key lighting creates strong shadows

questions.solution: High-key lighting is bright and even, with few shadows, creating a light mood
questions.hint: Think 'high' and bright

questions.text: What is the name for everyday sound effects, such as footsteps, created and recorded after filming to match the action? Give the term.
questions.solution: Foley is the art of recreating everyday sound effects in a studio, in time with the picture
questions.hint: It is named after Jack, a sound artist at Universal Studios

questions.text: Which of these is an example of non-diegetic sound?

options: A character's dialogue
The orchestral score that only the audience hears
A radio playing in a character's kitchen
The footsteps of a character walking
feedback: The characters can hear the radio, so it is diegetic

questions.solution: Non-diegetic sound, such as the film score, comes from outside the story world
questions.hint: Which sound could the characters not hear?

questions.text: Which lighting style uses strong shadows and contrast, and is often used in horror and film noir?

options: Low-key lighting
High-key lighting
Fill lighting
Natural daylight

questions.solution: Low-key lighting creates dark shadows and strong contrast, building mystery or fear
questions.hint: Think 'low' and dark

questions.text: What is the term for a sound that carries over a cut, linking the end of one scene to the start of the next? Give the term.
questions.solution: A sound bridge carries sound across a cut, smoothly linking two scenes
questions.hint: Think of something that crosses a gap to join two sides

questions.text: What is the difference between diegetic and non-diegetic sound?

options: Diegetic sound comes from the story world; non-diegetic sound is added for the audience only
Diegetic sound is music; non-diegetic sound is dialogue
Diegetic sound is recorded later; non-diegetic sound is recorded on set
Diegetic sound is loud; non-diegetic sound is quiet

questions.solution: Characters can hear diegetic sound; non-diegetic sound, such as the score, is for the audience only
questions.hint: Ask whether the characters can hear it

questions.text: In three-point lighting, which light is the main, brightest source on the subject?

options: Fill light
Back light
Practical light
Key light
feedback: The fill light is weaker and softens shadows
The back light separates the subject from the background

questions.solution: The key light is the main source; the fill light softens shadows and the back light separates the subject
questions.hint: It is the 'key' to the lighting set-up

questions.text: In three-point lighting, which light softens the shadows created by the main light? Give the term.

feedback.key light: The key light is the main light; a weaker light softens its shadows
feedback.back light: The back light sits behind the subject to separate it from the background
feedback.backlight: The back light sits behind the subject to separate it from the background

questions.solution: The fill light is a weaker light that softens the shadows made by the key light
questions.hint: It lightens the dark areas on the other side of the face

questions.text: In film, what is a prop?

options: An object in the scene that characters use or that dresses the set
A large light used outdoors
A type of camera support
A sound effect added later

questions.solution: Props are objects in the frame, used by characters or dressing the set
questions.hint: The word is short for 'property'

questions.text: What is the term for music that sounds happy or calm while something disturbing happens on screen, creating a clash? Give the term.

feedback.parallel sound: Parallel sound matches the mood of the images
feedback.parallel: Parallel sound matches the mood of the images

questions.solution: Contrapuntal sound contrasts with the mood of the images, which can unsettle the audience
questions.hint: The opposite term is 'parallel sound'

questions.text: Which part of mise-en-scène includes a character's clothing, hairstyle and make-up?

options: Costume, hair and make-up
Setting
Lighting
Editing

questions.solution: Costume, hair and make-up show character, status, period and change
questions.hint: Think about how the actor looks

questions.text: What is a recurring piece of music linked to a particular character or idea called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A leitmotif is a recurring musical idea linked to a character, place or idea
questions.hint: Think of the two-note music that signals the shark in Jaws

questions.text: In a horror film, a character walks down a corridor lit by a single flickering bulb, leaving deep shadows. What does this lighting create?

options: A cheerful, safe mood
Tension and fear, because the audience cannot see what is hidden
A sense of bright daytime
A comic, light-hearted tone

questions.solution: Low-key lighting with deep shadows hides parts of the frame, creating tension and fear
questions.hint: Think about what the shadows might hide

questions.text: A character hums a tune, and the same tune continues, played by an orchestra, as the film cuts to the next scene. What does this transition use?

options: Foley
Jump cut
Sound bridge
Ambient sound only
feedback: Foley is recreated sound effects such as footsteps

questions.solution: The music carries across the cut and links the scenes: a sound bridge
questions.hint: The sound continues across the cut

questions.text: In a scene set in a busy café, background chatter, clinking cups and traffic outside are heard quietly behind the dialogue. What is the specific name for this background sound of a location? Give the term.

feedback.diegetic: It is diegetic, but there is a more specific name for the background sound of a location
feedback.diegetic sound: It is diegetic, but there is a more specific name for the background sound of a location
feedback.foley: Foley is recreated sound effects for specific actions, such as footsteps

questions.solution: Ambient sound (atmos) is the background sound of a location, which makes the setting feel real
questions.hint: The term comes from a word meaning 'surrounding'

questions.text: A film uses a dull, grey colour palette in a story about a lonely office worker. What does the colour most likely suggest?

options: Joy and celebration
That the film is a musical
That the scene takes place in summer
Sadness and a lack of excitement in his life

questions.solution: Grey, desaturated colours connote dullness and sadness, reflecting his lonely life
questions.hint: Think about the connotations of grey

questions.text: A gangster film opens in a cramped, dark basement full of crates of stolen money. Which element of mise-en-scène is the basement? Give the term.

feedback.props: Props are objects within the scene; the basement is the place itself
feedback.prop: Props are objects within the scene; the basement is the place itself

questions.solution: The basement is the setting, the place where the action happens
questions.hint: It is the place, not an object within it

questions.text: A character in a crime film is lit from below, so shadows stretch upwards across her face. What is this effect usually used to suggest?

options: That the character is a hero
That it is a sunny morning
Something sinister or threatening about the character
That the scene is a flashback

questions.solution: Underlighting distorts the face with upward shadows, suggesting something sinister
questions.hint: Think of someone holding a torch under their chin to tell a ghost story

questions.text: Read this description: 'Bright, even lighting; a pastel-coloured bedroom; an upbeat pop song the character sings along to.' Which genre do these choices most likely suggest?

options: Horror
Film noir
War film
Teen or romantic comedy

questions.solution: High-key lighting, pastel colours and an upbeat diegetic song suggest a light-hearted comedy
questions.hint: Work out the mood of the lighting, colour and music, then match it to a genre

questions.text: Read this description: 'A detective sits in a dark office; light through the window blinds casts striped shadows; rain falls outside; a slow saxophone plays on the soundtrack.' Which film style does this mise-en-scène suggest?

options: Musical
Western
Teen comedy
Film noir

questions.solution: Low-key lighting, striped shadows, rain, a detective and moody jazz are classic film noir conventions
questions.hint: Think of the dark, shadowy crime films of the 1940s

questions.text: Read this: 'The score swells as the hero reaches the summit, but the climber beside him cannot hear it.' Is the score diegetic or non-diegetic? Give the term.

feedback.diegetic: The other character cannot hear it, so it is not part of the story world
feedback.diegetic sound: The other character cannot hear it, so it is not part of the story world

questions.solution: The other climber cannot hear the score, so it is outside the story world: non-diegetic
questions.hint: Can the characters in the scene hear it?

questions.text: A director wants the audience to feel that a calm family dinner hides a secret. Which choice would create this?

options: Bright high-key lighting with upbeat pop music
A comic sound effect each time someone speaks
Warm lighting with a low, tense note of music underneath
A cheerful, fast orchestral score

questions.solution: The warm lighting shows calm on the surface, while a low, tense note hints that something is wrong
questions.hint: The scene needs something calm and something uneasy at the same time

questions.text: Read this: 'In the final shot, the hero's white costume is torn and stained with mud.' What does this change in costume most likely show?

options: The film is set in the future
The character has been changed by struggle or conflict
The character is about to get married
The scene is a dream

questions.solution: A once-clean costume now torn and dirty shows what the character has been through
questions.hint: Compare the costume now with how it looked at the start

questions.text: Explain how lighting and sound could be combined to build suspense in a horror scene.

rubric.model_answer: Low-key lighting would leave much of the room in shadow, so the audience cannot see what might be hiding, and a single source of light would create harsh contrasts. A slow, quiet non-diegetic score with long silences, broken by small diegetic sounds such as a creaking floorboard, would make the audience listen closely and expect something to happen.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: a lighting choice (e.g. low-key, shadows, a single source)
1 mark: the effect of the lighting on suspense
1 mark: a sound choice (e.g. score, silence, diegetic effects)
1 mark: the effect of the sound on suspense

questions.solution: Shadows hide threats; quiet music, silence and sudden small sounds keep the audience on edge
questions.hint: Deal with lighting first, then sound, then say how they work together

questions.text: Which statement about mise-en-scène is accurate?

options: It refers only to the camera angles used in a film
It means the music chosen after editing
The term comes from theatre and means 'putting into the scene'; it covers everything placed in the frame
It is the name for the film's opening titles

questions.solution: Mise-en-scène is a French theatre term, 'putting into the scene', covering everything in the frame
questions.hint: Translate the French phrase

questions.text: Why do sound designers often record Foley rather than using the sound recorded on set?

options: Foley is cheaper because no recording is needed
On-set sound is often unclear, so Foley gives clean, controlled effects that match the action
Foley is only used for music
Laws require all sound to be recorded later

questions.solution: On-set recordings focus on dialogue and pick up noise, so Foley artists recreate clear effects in a studio
questions.hint: Think about how noisy a film set is

questions.text: Which statement about high-key and low-key lighting is accurate?

options: High-key lighting reduces shadows and suits light moods; low-key lighting creates contrast and suits dark moods
Both always create exactly the same mood
High-key lighting is darker than low-key lighting
Low-key lighting is mostly used in children's films

questions.solution: High-key lighting is bright with few shadows; low-key lighting has strong contrast and shadows
questions.hint: Link 'high' with bright and 'low' with dark

questions.text: Why might a director play contrapuntal music over a violent scene?

options: To make the violence seem realistic by matching its mood
Because film music must always be happy
To tell the audience that the film is a musical
The clash between music and images can unsettle the audience and make the scene more disturbing
feedback: Matching the mood is parallel sound, not contrapuntal

questions.solution: Contrapuntal music clashes with the images, which can make a scene more unsettling
questions.hint: What does 'contrapuntal' mean: matching or clashing?

questions.text: Which statement about diegetic sound is accurate?

options: It can be on-screen or off-screen, as long as its source is in the story world
It must always be music
It can never be heard by the characters
It is always written by the film's composer

questions.solution: Diegetic sound can come from off-screen, such as a knock at a door we cannot see
questions.hint: Think about a sound the characters hear from outside the frame

questions.text: Explain how a character's costume can tell the audience about them. Use an example of your own.

rubric.model_answer: Costume communicates status, personality and change. For example, a businesswoman in a sharp, dark tailored suit connotes power and control, while later in the film she wears loose, colourful clothes, showing she has relaxed and changed her priorities. Colour, fit and condition of clothing all carry connotations the audience reads quickly.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: an aspect of character shown by costume (e.g. status, personality, job, period)
1 mark: a relevant example of a costume detail
1 mark: the connotation of the detail explained
1 mark: development, e.g. a change of costume showing a change in the character

questions.solution: Colour, fit and condition of costume show status, personality and change
questions.hint: Choose one character and describe their clothes, then what they suggest

questions.text: What is the term for the main character of a film, whose goals drive the story? Give the term.

feedback.antagonist: The antagonist is the character who opposes the main character

questions.solution: The protagonist is the central character whose goals drive the plot
questions.hint: It is the opposite of the antagonist

questions.text: What is iconography in film genre?

options: The familiar objects, settings and costumes that signal a genre
The order of events in a story
The sound added after filming
The study of film audiences

questions.solution: Iconography is the visual signs of a genre, such as the Stetsons and saloons of a Western
questions.hint: The word contains 'icon', meaning an image

questions.text: What is an auteur?

options: A director whose films show a distinctive personal style and recurring themes
A person who writes film reviews
A cinema owner
An actor who does their own stunts

questions.solution: An auteur is a director seen as the 'author' of their films, with a recognisable style
questions.hint: The word is French for 'author'

questions.text: What is the name for the character who opposes the main character and creates conflict? Give the term.

feedback.protagonist: The protagonist is the main character, not the one who opposes them

questions.solution: The antagonist opposes the protagonist and creates conflict
questions.hint: This character works against the main character

questions.text: In the three-act structure, what happens in Act One?

options: The setup: the characters, setting and main problem are introduced
The final battle and resolution
The end credits roll
The story is told backwards

questions.solution: Act One sets up the characters, the world and the problem; Act Two is confrontation; Act Three is resolution
questions.hint: Think about what has to happen first in any story

questions.text: Which of these is typical iconography of the Western genre?

options: Spaceships, robots and lasers
Cowboy hats, horses and saloons
Haunted houses and candles
Tuxedos, casinos and gadgets
feedback: That is science fiction iconography
That is horror iconography

questions.solution: Stetsons, horses, saloons and deserts are classic Western iconography
questions.hint: Think of the American frontier

questions.text: What is the term for a film that combines two or more genres, such as a sci-fi horror? Give the term.
questions.solution: A hybrid genre film mixes the conventions of two or more genres
questions.hint: The same word is used for a car that runs on both petrol and electricity

questions.text: What is the difference between a film's story and its plot?

options: The story is all the events in time order; the plot is how they are arranged and shown in the film
The story is shown on screen; the plot exists only in the script
The story is the music; the plot is the dialogue
There is no difference: they mean exactly the same thing

questions.solution: The story is every event in time order, including ones we only infer; the plot is the order and way the film shows them
questions.hint: A film with flashbacks shows events out of order

questions.text: What is a subgenre?

options: A film that has no genre
A genre made only for television
The music used in a genre film
A smaller, more specific category within a genre, such as the slasher film within horror

questions.solution: A subgenre is a more specific category inside a broader genre
questions.hint: 'Sub' means under or within

questions.text: What is the term for a story told in time order, from beginning to end, without jumping around in time? Give the term.

feedback.non-linear: A non-linear narrative jumps around in time, for example with flashbacks
feedback.non-linear narrative: A non-linear narrative jumps around in time, for example with flashbacks

questions.solution: A linear narrative presents events in chronological order
questions.hint: It moves forward in a straight line

questions.text: Who is most closely linked with the idea of the 'male gaze' in film spectatorship?

options: Tzvetan Todorov
Laura Mulvey
Steve Neale
Vladimir Propp
feedback: Todorov is known for narrative theory
Steve Neale is known for genre theory

questions.solution: Laura Mulvey introduced the male gaze in 1975
questions.hint: She is a British feminist film theorist

questions.text: In the three-act structure, what is the name for the event early in the story that sets the main plot in motion? Give the term.
questions.solution: The inciting incident sets the story in motion by disrupting the protagonist's normal life
questions.hint: It provokes, or sets off, the action

questions.text: What is the difference between an open ending and a closed ending?

options: An open ending leaves questions unresolved; a closed ending ties up the main storylines
An open ending is always happy; a closed ending is always sad
An open ending has no music; a closed ending has a song
An open ending is in colour; a closed ending is in black and white

questions.solution: Closed endings resolve the story; open endings leave questions for the audience
questions.hint: Think about whether the story is 'closed off'

questions.text: Which British film theorist described genres as 'instances of repetition and difference'? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Steve Neale argued that genres work through repetition of conventions and difference
questions.hint: He wrote the book 'Genre' (1980)

questions.text: A film opens with a character waking in a hospital with no memory, then jumps back to show how she got there. Which narrative technique is used?

options: Flash-forward
Cross-cutting
Linear narrative
Flashback

questions.solution: Jumping back in time to show earlier events is a flashback, making the narrative non-linear
questions.hint: Is the film jumping forwards or backwards in time?

questions.text: In a fantasy film, the audience knows that the villain is hiding in the castle, but the hero does not. What is this called?

options: Red herring
Open ending
Dramatic irony
MacGuffin
feedback: A red herring is a misleading clue

questions.solution: Dramatic irony is when the audience knows something a character does not
questions.hint: The audience knows more than the hero

questions.text: A mystery film points the audience towards a suspicious butler who turns out to be innocent. What is this misleading clue called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A red herring is a false clue that misleads the audience
questions.hint: It is named after a strong-smelling fish

questions.text: A film tells its story only through what one character knows, so the audience discovers clues at the same time as she does. What type of narration is this?

options: Unrestricted (omniscient) narration
Parallel editing
Restricted narration
Contrapuntal sound
feedback: Unrestricted narration lets the audience know more than any one character

questions.solution: Restricted narration limits the audience to what one character knows, often building mystery
questions.hint: Is the audience's knowledge limited or unlimited?

questions.text: Across many films, a director uses symmetrical framing, pastel colours and quirky characters, so audiences recognise the style at once. Which theory treats a director like this as the 'author' of their films? Give the name of the theory.
questions.solution: Auteur theory sees the director as the author of a film, with a recognisable style across their work
questions.hint: The term comes from the French word for 'author'

questions.text: A science fiction film includes a robot, a spaceship and laser weapons. What do these elements show about genre?

options: They are examples of non-diegetic sound
They are iconography that signals the sci-fi genre
They show the film is a documentary
They prove the film has a linear narrative

questions.solution: Robots, spaceships and lasers are iconography of science fiction
questions.hint: These are visual objects associated with a genre

questions.text: Read this summary: 'Act 1: a young chef dreams of opening a restaurant. Act 2: she loses her savings and her business partner leaves. Act 3: she wins a cooking contest and opens the restaurant.' Which part of the three-act structure is Act 2?

options: The setup, where characters are introduced
The confrontation, where obstacles increase
The resolution, where problems are solved
The epilogue, after the credits

questions.solution: Act Two is the confrontation: the protagonist faces growing obstacles before the resolution
questions.hint: Act 2 is where things go wrong for her

questions.text: Read this: 'A film begins with the hero arrested for a robbery, then shows the week before the robbery, then returns to his trial.' How is the narrative structured?

options: Linear, in strict time order
In real time, with no edits
Non-linear, using a flashback
As a montage of the future

questions.solution: Starting at the arrest, going back a week, then forward again is a non-linear structure with a flashback
questions.hint: Put the three events in time order and compare that with the order shown

questions.text: Read this: 'A Western features a sheriff, a lone gunfighter, a saloon and a showdown. A later film keeps all of these but sets them on a distant planet.' Steve Neale said genres work through repetition and what? Give the word.
questions.solution: Neale argued that genres repeat familiar conventions but also add difference to stay fresh
questions.hint: The second film changes something while keeping the rest

questions.text: Read this: 'Many audience members cheered when the villain was defeated, but some felt sorry for him because of his tragic backstory.' What does this show about spectatorship?

options: All spectators respond to a film in exactly the same way
Different spectators can respond to the same film in different ways
Audiences never feel sympathy for villains
The film must have been a documentary

questions.solution: Spectators bring their own experiences and values, so responses to the same film can differ
questions.hint: Compare the two groups' responses

questions.text: Read this: 'In a romantic comedy, two characters meet, dislike each other, are forced to work together and finally fall in love.' Which term describes familiar, repeated story patterns like this in a genre?

options: Iconography
Mise-en-scène
Cinematography
Narrative conventions
feedback: Iconography is about visual objects and settings, not story patterns

questions.solution: Repeated story patterns are narrative conventions; iconography is the visual objects of a genre
questions.hint: This is about the story, not about what is seen in the frame

questions.text: Explain how a genre film can both follow and break genre conventions. Use an example of your own.

rubric.model_answer: A genre film follows conventions so the audience recognises it: a superhero film has a hero with special powers, a villain and a final battle. It may also break conventions to surprise the audience, for example by making the hero morally flawed or letting the villain win. This mix of familiar and new, which Steve Neale called repetition and difference, keeps the genre fresh.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: an example of a convention that is followed
1 mark: why following conventions matters (recognition, expectations)
1 mark: an example of a convention that is broken or changed
1 mark: why breaking conventions matters (surprise, freshness, repetition and difference)

questions.solution: Genres repeat familiar conventions but change some of them to surprise audiences
questions.hint: Pick one genre and list its usual conventions first

questions.text: Which statement about auteur theory is accurate?

options: It treats the director as the main creative 'author', though critics note films are made by large teams
It argues that the screenwriter alone decides how a film looks
It says only silent films can have auteurs
It was created to describe video game design

questions.solution: Auteur theory sees the director as the author of a film; critics point out that filmmaking is collaborative
questions.hint: Who is the 'author' in auteur theory?

questions.text: Why do film studios often prefer to make genre films?

options: Genre films are exempt from age certificates
Genre films need no marketing at all
Genre films are always cheaper than any other film
Familiar genres attract audiences who know what to expect, which reduces financial risk

questions.solution: Genres come with ready-made audiences and expectations, which makes them a safer investment
questions.hint: Think about money and risk

questions.text: Which statement about Laura Mulvey's 'male gaze' is accurate?

options: She argued that only men watch films
She invented the three-act structure
She argued that genre conventions never change
She argued mainstream cinema often positions the spectator to look at women from a male point of view

questions.solution: Mulvey argued that classical cinema often frames women as objects of a male look
questions.hint: Think about whose point of view the camera adopts

questions.text: Why might a film use a non-linear narrative?

options: To create mystery or reveal information in a surprising order
Because non-linear films do not need editing
To make sure the audience can always predict the ending
Because age ratings require it

questions.solution: Telling events out of order can create mystery, surprise or new connections between events
questions.hint: Think about the effect of seeing events out of order

questions.text: Which statement about the three-act structure is accurate?

options: It requires every film to be exactly three hours long
It was used only for silent films and has since been abandoned
It divides a story into setup, confrontation and resolution, and is widely used in mainstream films
It means a film must have three protagonists

questions.solution: The three-act structure (setup, confrontation, resolution) is common in mainstream, especially Hollywood, films
questions.hint: Name the three acts

questions.text: Explain how a film can position the spectator to sympathise with a character.

rubric.model_answer: The film can align the spectator with a character by giving them the most screen time, close-ups and point-of-view shots, so we share their experiences and feelings. Restricted narration means we learn things only when they do. Music, such as a gentle score in sad moments, and dialogue revealing their motives or backstory, encourage us to care about them, even if they make mistakes.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: camera choices (e.g. close-ups, point-of-view shots) create alignment
1 mark: narration or screen time shares the character's experience
1 mark: sound or music encouraging emotion
1 mark: backstory or motives building sympathy

questions.solution: Camera, narration, music and backstory can all align the spectator with a character
questions.hint: Think about camera, sound and story in turn

questions.text: In which year did the Lumière brothers hold their first public film screening for a paying audience in Paris? Give the year.
questions.solution: The Lumière brothers showed their films to a paying audience in Paris on 28 December 1895
questions.hint: It was in the mid-1890s, in late December

questions.text: What were intertitles in silent films?

options: Musical instruments played in the cinema
Printed text shown between shots to give dialogue or describe the action
Coloured filters on the projector
Posters displayed outside the cinema

questions.solution: Intertitles were cards of printed text that gave dialogue or narration in silent films
questions.hint: Silent films had no recorded speech, so how did viewers read the dialogue?

questions.text: Which 1927 film is usually credited as the first feature film with synchronised spoken dialogue scenes, starting the 'talkie' era?

options: Metropolis
The Wizard of Oz
The Jazz Singer
Citizen Kane
feedback: Metropolis (1927) was a silent German film
The Wizard of Oz came out in 1939

questions.solution: The Jazz Singer (1927) used synchronised songs and some dialogue, launching the era of sound films
questions.hint: Its title refers to a style of music

questions.text: What is the name for the stage of the film industry that gets a film to audiences by marketing it and arranging where and when it is shown? Give the term.

feedback.exhibition: Exhibition is the actual showing of the film, for example in cinemas
feedback.production: Production is the making of the film

questions.solution: Distribution links production and exhibition: marketing the film and arranging its release
questions.hint: It sits between production and exhibition

questions.text: Which BBFC certificate means a film is suitable for all ages?

options: PG (Parental Guidance)
U (Universal)

questions.solution: U stands for Universal: suitable for audiences aged four years and over, so for everyone
questions.hint: Its letter stands for a word meaning 'for everyone'

questions.text: What does CGI stand for?

options: Camera-guided illumination
Cinema graphics interface
Computer-generated imagery
Colour grading instruction

questions.solution: CGI stands for computer-generated imagery
questions.hint: The C stands for computer

questions.text: What is the name for the stage of the film industry in which films are shown to audiences, for example in cinemas? Give the term.

feedback.distribution: Distribution is marketing the film and arranging its release; showing it is the next stage

questions.solution: Exhibition is the showing of films to audiences, for example in cinemas or on other platforms
questions.hint: Think about where an art gallery puts its pictures on show

questions.text: What was the Hollywood studio system?

options: Large studios controlled production, distribution and cinemas, with actors and crews on long contracts
Small independent companies made low-budget films
The government made all films in America
A system for giving films age certificates

questions.solution: In the studio era, major studios owned the whole chain and kept stars and staff on long-term contracts
questions.hint: Think about who controlled every stage of filmmaking

questions.text: Which of these studios was one of Hollywood's 'Big Five' in the studio era?

options: Pixar
Netflix
MGM (Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer)
Aardman Animations

questions.solution: The Big Five were MGM, Paramount, Warner Bros., 20th Century Fox and RKO
questions.hint: The other three companies were founded long after the studio era

questions.text: What is the term for a film made outside the major studio system, usually with a lower budget? Give the term.
questions.solution: Independent (indie) films are made outside the major studios, usually on lower budgets
questions.hint: It is made without the backing of a major studio

questions.text: What is the difference between the BBFC certificates 12A and 12?

options: 12A is for home video; 12 is for cinema
12A means the film is animated; 12 means it is live action
There is no difference
12A is for cinema (under-12s only with an adult); 12 is for home video, which under-12s may not buy

questions.solution: 12A applies in cinemas, where under-12s can watch with an adult; the 12 certificate applies to video releases
questions.hint: The A stands for 'accompanied'

questions.text: Which 1995 Pixar film was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation? Give the title.
questions.solution: Toy Story (1995) was the first fully computer-animated feature film
questions.hint: It follows a cowboy doll and a space ranger toy

questions.text: What is a multiplex cinema?

options: A cinema with many screens in one building
A cinema that only shows silent films
A film shown on several TV channels at once
A camera that films in 3D

questions.solution: A multiplex has many screens, so it can show many films at once
questions.hint: 'Multi' means many

questions.text: What name is given to the period of American filmmaking from the late 1960s to around 1980, when young directors such as Scorsese and Coppola gained more creative control? Give the term.
questions.solution: New Hollywood (the American New Wave) gave young directors more control from the late 1960s
questions.hint: It followed the decline of the old studio system

questions.text: A distributor opens a film in a few cinemas in big cities, then expands to more cinemas as good reviews spread. What is this release strategy called?

options: Saturation (wide) release
Day-and-date release
Platform release
Direct-to-video release
feedback: A saturation release opens on as many screens as possible at once

questions.solution: A platform release starts small and widens as word of mouth grows
questions.hint: The film builds up from a small base

questions.text: A blockbuster opens on thousands of screens on the same day, backed by huge TV and online advertising. What is this release strategy called?

options: Platform release
Limited festival release
Saturation (wide) release
Silent release

questions.solution: A saturation release opens everywhere at once to maximise the opening weekend
questions.hint: The market is 'flooded' with the film

questions.text: A film is released in cinemas and on a streaming service on the same day. What is this called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A day-and-date release puts a film in cinemas and on home platforms at the same time
questions.hint: The name is a phrase with the word 'and' in the middle

questions.text: In the 1930s, a studio owns a film, the company that distributes it and the cinemas that show it. What is this an example of?

options: Vertical integration
Horizontal integration
Independent production
Day-and-date release

questions.solution: Owning production, distribution and exhibition is vertical integration
questions.hint: The company owns different stages of the same chain

questions.text: A parent sees that a film is rated PG. What do the letters PG stand for? Give the words.
questions.solution: PG means Parental Guidance: general viewing, but some scenes may be unsuitable for young children
questions.hint: The P refers to parents

questions.text: A film needs a dinosaur that interacts with real actors, so the creature is created on computers and added in post-production. Which technology is being used?

options: Stop-motion with clay models only
Silent intertitles
CGI
Deep focus

questions.solution: Creating images on computers and adding them in post-production is CGI
questions.hint: The creature was made on computers

questions.text: Read this timeline: '1927: The Jazz Singer. 1948: the Paramount Decision. Late 1960s: New Hollywood begins.' What did the 1948 Paramount Decision do?

options: It introduced synchronised sound to Hollywood
It created the BBFC
It forced the big studios to sell their cinema chains, weakening the studio system
It banned colour films in America
feedback: Synchronised sound arrived in 1927 with The Jazz Singer

questions.solution: The 1948 US Supreme Court ruling made the studios sell their cinemas, ending their vertical integration
questions.hint: Think about what happened to the studio system after 1948

questions.text: Read this: 'A low-budget film premieres at a festival, wins a prize, and is then bought by a distributor.' Why are film festivals important for independent films?

options: They attract attention, reviews and distributors without a large marketing budget
They give every film an automatic BBFC certificate
They replace the need for exhibition
They are only for studio blockbusters

questions.solution: Festivals give independent films publicity, reviews and the chance to be picked up by distributors
questions.hint: What did the festival lead to in the example?

questions.text: Read this: 'In the late 1920s, silent films were quickly replaced by films with recorded sound.' What was the popular name for these new sound films? Give the term.
questions.solution: Sound films were nicknamed 'talkies' because audiences could now hear actors speak
questions.hint: The name comes from the fact that audiences could now hear actors speak

questions.text: Read this: 'A film took £40 million at the box office worldwide but cost £60 million to make and market.' What does this suggest?

options: On box-office figures alone, the film lost money
The film made a profit of £20 million
The film exactly broke even
The film made a profit of £100 million

questions.solution: £40 million in minus £60 million in costs is a £20 million shortfall on box-office figures alone
questions.hint: Compare the money taken with the money spent

questions.text: Read this: 'In the 1950s, studios introduced widescreen formats such as CinemaScope and experimented with 3D.' What were they most likely responding to?

options: The invention of synchronised sound
The arrival of streaming services
The end of the First World War
Competition from television, which was keeping audiences at home
feedback: Synchronised sound arrived in the late 1920s
Streaming arrived in the 21st century

questions.solution: Studios offered bigger, more spectacular images to compete with television in the 1950s
questions.hint: What new technology appeared in many homes in the 1950s?

questions.text: Explain how the arrival of streaming has changed film distribution and exhibition.

rubric.model_answer: Streaming services let audiences watch films at home on many devices, so the cinema is no longer the only first window. Some films are released on streaming services and in cinemas on the same day, or only online, which shortens the gap between cinema and home release. Streaming companies also produce and distribute their own films, using data about viewers to decide what to make and recommend.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: viewing at home on many devices as a change in exhibition
1 mark: shorter release windows, day-and-date or online-only releases
1 mark: streaming companies acting as producers and distributors
1 mark: use of viewer data or recommendations

questions.solution: Streaming changes where films are watched, when they are released and who distributes them
questions.hint: Think about where, when and how people now watch new films

questions.text: Which statement about classical Hollywood cinema is accurate?

options: It rejected all genre films
It was made mainly by independent directors with tiny budgets
It mostly used jump cuts and non-linear stories
It favoured continuity editing and clear, goal-driven narratives with resolved endings

questions.solution: Classical Hollywood used invisible continuity editing and clear cause-and-effect stories with closure
questions.hint: Think about the studio era and its storytelling

questions.text: Why did the French New Wave of the late 1950s and 1960s influence later filmmakers?

options: It introduced synchronised sound
It invented Technicolor
It created the Hollywood star system
Its directors broke rules with jump cuts, handheld cameras and location shooting

questions.solution: Directors such as Godard and Truffaut broke classical rules, inspiring filmmakers around the world
questions.hint: Think about Godard's Breathless (1960)

questions.text: Which statement about the BBFC's age ratings is accurate?

options: They classify films by content, such as violence, language and frightening scenes, and set age limits
They are decided by the film's director
They only apply to video games
They rate films on how good they are

questions.solution: BBFC ratings are based on content issues such as violence, language and threat, not on quality
questions.hint: What does the BBFC look at when it rates a film?

questions.text: Why is Jaws (1975) often called the first summer blockbuster?

options: It opened widely with heavy TV advertising and earned record box-office takings
It was the first film with sound
It was the first fully computer-animated film
It was released only at film festivals

questions.solution: Jaws combined a wide release with national TV advertising and became the highest-earning film of its time
questions.hint: Think about how it was marketed and released

questions.text: Which statement about CGI is accurate?

options: It was used in the earliest silent films of the 1890s
It means a film has no actors
It allows filmmakers to create images that would be impossible or too costly to film for real
It can only be used in animated films

questions.solution: CGI creates images digitally, from whole creatures to crowds and landscapes, that could not be filmed practically
questions.hint: Think about what computers let filmmakers create

questions.text: Explain why the Hollywood studio system declined after the 1940s.

rubric.model_answer: The 1948 Paramount Decision forced the major studios to sell their cinema chains, ending vertical integration and block booking, so they lost guaranteed screens for their films. At the same time, television kept many audiences at home, cinema attendance fell, and stars and directors increasingly worked freelance rather than on long-term contracts.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: the 1948 Paramount Decision
1 mark: loss of cinema chains, ending vertical integration or block booking
1 mark: competition from television and falling attendance
1 mark: stars and directors leaving long-term studio contracts

questions.solution: The Paramount Decision, television and the end of long contracts weakened the studios
questions.hint: Think about a court ruling, a new technology and the stars themselves
